title: Operator Collaboration & Shared-State Contract (runtime operators)
author: Avery Li
body:
Overview:

This document defines the collaboration contract between platform operators who manage the LLM runtime (prefetch, KV cache, batching, allocator) and platform services that depend on shared in-memory or metastore state. The goal is to reduce oncall churn, make handoffs deterministic, and provide a single source of truth for operator actions that affect runtime health and tenant isolation.

Audience:
- Platform operators (primary)
- Service owners and oncall engineers (secondary)
- SRE and infra ops (tertiary)

Goals:
- Define a compact, unambiguous shared-state schema and ownership model.
- Provide standard preflight checks and safe mutation patterns for operators.
- Describe handoff and takeover procedures for rapid incident response.
- Standardize instrumented signals and dashboards to detect contract violations.

Scope and non‑goals:
- Scope: coordination patterns around KV prefix caches, tenant warmsets, allocator credits, and model-variant routing metadata.
- Non-goal: replacing higher-level orchestration policies (e.g., scheduler decisions) — this contract complements them.

Contract overview (plain language):
- Shared state is a small set of canonical keys in the runtime metastore. Services may read keys freely. Any operator or automated process that mutates keys must:
  1) Record intent via the operator-ledger entry (see "Operator Ledger" below),
  2) Run the preflight checks (Section: Preflight),
  3) Execute the mutation via the approved CLI or orchestration endpoint, and
  4) Post a postcondition note and alert the owning service channel if the change is nontrivial.

Operator Ledger (audit + intent registration):
- The ledger is a single append-only stream stored in the internal metadata service. For ad-hoc operational changes, write a ledger record before mutating shared state. Each ledger record must include: author, timestamp, target_key(s), intended_mutation, expected_impact, rollback_plan, and a correlation_id.

Ledger record example (JSON):
{
  "author": "avery.li@redwood.ai",
  "timestamp": "2025-03-12T09:42:00Z",
  "target_keys": ["kv-prefix/tenant-123/warmset"],
  "intended_mutation": "evict-prefix",
  "expected_impact": "approx 20% increase in token-latency P95 for tenant-123 for up to 60s",
  "rollback_plan": "re-add prefix from snapshot: snapshot://prefetch/2025-03-12/tenant-123",
  "correlation_id": "op-20250312-0942-tenant123-evict"
}

Preflight checklist (must pass before manual/CLI mutation):
1) Confirm ledger entry is present and visible in the operator dashboard.
2) Validate the change against the service compatibility matrix: ensure tenant-123 is allowed to be evicted during the current maintenance window.
3) Check token budget and allocator credits: operation must not cause allocator to drop below the safety floor (see thresholds).
4) Synthetic load simulation (where applicable): run a 30s synthetic prefix-read trace in the staging overlay.
5) Stakeholder notification: add an @mention to the service Slack channel and wait the configured quiet-period (default 90s) unless an emergency takeover is declared.

Safe mutation patterns (common ops):
- Evicting a KV prefix:
  - Use: rld-cli runtime evict --target-prefix tenant-123/warmset --ledger-cid op-...
  - Steps: preflight, dry-run (no-op), execute, monitor P95 token-latency for 5 minutes, rollback if >2x baseline for >2 consecutive minutes.
- Warmset reseed:
  - Use: rld-cli runtime reseed --source snapshot://prefetch/... --target tenant-123
  - Steps: schedule during low-traffic window, notify service, perform reseed with rate-limiting, confirm metrics.
- Rebalancing shard ownership:
  - Use: rld-cli allocator reassign --shard s42 --from nodeA --to nodeB --ledger-cid op-...
  - Steps: drain nodeA with soft-eviction flag, monitor hot-queue lengths, uncordon nodeB on success.

Shared-state schema (canonical keys and semantics):
| Key pattern | Purpose | Owner | Mutability | Safety note |
|-------------|---------|-------|-----------|-------------|
| kv-prefix/{tenant}/warmset | list of warm keys/prefixes used by prefetch | prefetch-service | operator or automated prefetch | Mutate only via reseed/evict contract |
| allocator/tenant/{tenant}/credits | soft-credit balance for burst capacity | allocator | allocator-service writes; operators may patch | Do not undercut safety_floor (see thresholds) |
| routing/variant/{model}/preferred | hints for model-variant fallback routing | serving-runtime | product or serving-runtime | Operators may adjust for emergency fallbacks |

Important thresholds (operational safety):
- allocator safety_floor: 0.15 (15% of baseline credits) — manual operator patches must not reduce below floor.
- warmset min_coverage: 70% — reseed attempts should aim for >=70% of historical prefix hit rate.
- tenant throttle_warning_p95: increase >1.8x baseline triggers automated rollback.

Dashboards and required signals (owner: observability-team):
- Operator Ledger stream: real-time tail view, filters by correlation_id, author, and key.
- Key mutation heatmap: frequency of mutations by prefix/tenant over 24h and 7d.
- Preflight validation success rate: % of manual attempts that pass preflight. Target >=95%.
- Mutation impact window: automated view of token-latency P50/P95 and error-rate for 15m before and 60m after mutation.
- Canary simulation results: synthetic workload pass/fail for reseed operations.

Oncall handoff and takeover (short procedure):
1) Morning shift: primary oncall posts a digest to #ops-shift with open ledger entries and pending mutations.
2) Incoming engineer reviews ledger tail, validates any running leader-correlation IDs, and explicitly acknowledges takeover by adding an "acknowledged-by" ledger entry.
3) If an emergency takeover is required (e.g., global cache thrash): the incoming oncall raises the emergency tag on the ledger record and runs the emergency mutation flow (skip quiet period).
4) Post-incident: primary writes a postmortem summary entry in the ledger and files a short blameless retrospective (see Retrospective template below).

Emergency mutation flow (allowed only when safety automation is offline or oncall discretion):
1) Create a ledger record with emergency=true and justify with concrete telemetry links.
2) Execute the minimum-change action (evict smallest prefix, disable prefetch for specific tenant) with explicit rollback command ready.
3) Notify pager and the product owner channel with correlation_id and metric links.
4) Immediately schedule a post-incident review within 72 hours.

Operator CLI (approved commands and examples):
- rld-cli runtime evict --target-prefix <prefix> --ledger-cid <cid> --dry-run\- rld-cli runtime reseed --source <snapshot> --target-tenant <tenant> --rate-limit 100/s\- rld-cli allocator patch-credits --tenant <tenant> --delta -500 --ledger-cid <cid>

Monitoring queries (Prometheus-esque pseudo queries):
- token_latency_p95{tenant="tenant-123"} > 2 * baseline_token_latency_p95\- kv_prefix_evictions_total{prefix=~"tenant-.*"} by (tenant)

Rollout and enforcement plan:
- Phase 0 (pilot, 4 weeks): opt-in teams (prefetch, allocator) adopt ledger usage; dashboards enabled in staging.
- Phase 1 (guardrails, 8 weeks): enforce preflight checks by gating CLI commands behind validation service; automated ledger audit alerts created.
- Phase 2 (graduation): ledger becomes required metadata for any shared-state mutation; failures create immediate rollback tasks and SLO-incurred alerts.

Retrospective template (post-change):
- Title: concise change summary
- Timeline: key timestamps (ledger write, mutation start, observed impact)
- Metrics: P50/P95, error-rate, cold-start counts, token-cost delta
- Root cause / contributing factors
- Actions: owner, due date, verification steps

Ownership and escalation matrix:
- Prefetch service oncall: first responder for warmset semantics issues.
- Allocator oncall: first responder for credits and capacity patch requests.
- Platform operator rotation: only operators listed in the ledger author field may perform manual mutations; escalation to senior operator if unsure.

Open questions and future work:
- Formalize a small HTTP mutation API that only accepts operations with an attached, validated ledger entry.
- Add automated rollback playbooks that can be triggered via the ledger correlation_id.
- Evaluate storing small warmset snapshots in a compact tier for faster reseed.

Appendix A: Sample post-change notification (Slack snippet):
"Operator note: applied eviction op-20250312-0942-tenant123-evict to kv-prefix/tenant-123/warmset. Expected latency increase: +20% P95 for ~60s. Monitoring: https://dashboards.internal/ops/mutation/op-20250312-0942. Rollback: rld-cli runtime reseed --source snapshot://prefetch/2025-03-12/tenant-123 --ledger-cid op-20250312-0942-rollback"

Appendix B: Quick recovery commands:
- Re-add prefix from snapshot:
  - rld-cli runtime reseed --source snapshot://prefetch/2025-03-12/tenant-123 --target-tenant tenant-123 --ledger-cid <cid>
- Emergency allocator credit top-up:
  - rld-cli allocator patch-credits --tenant tenant-123 --delta 1000 --ledger-cid <cid>

Appendix C: Retrospective example (short):
- Incident: reseed caused 3x P95 increase for tenant-217 for 7 minutes.
- Cause: reseed was run without synthetic canary due to misconfigured staging overlay.
- Action items:
  1) Add mandatory synthetic canary step to preflight (owner: observability, due: 2025-03-19).
  2) Add validation to the CLI to reject reseed if staging overlay is unreachable (owner: runtime-team, due: 2025-03-26).
